title: The walking requirements judge replaces the 96-case scorer
summary: An audit of the 96 historical cases found 5 feasible for the robot as built, 31 unverified on torque, 51 limited only by the 0.35 rad action box and the 2.0 rad/s slew cap, and 9 unreachable from the declared stance; none ran at the mission speed. The scorer that owned them is deleted with its 437 lines, the probe suite, the three evaluation scopes and the nine evidence flags. The evaluation now has one path: configs/walking_requirements.json enumerates 21 cases (stand, 16 walks, 2 turns, 2 arcs, each held 20 s then stopped), the runner records one native trial per case, and the judge measures drift, stopping distance, tilt and applied torque against the file. The compatibility receipt binds the judge and requires every case recorded, not passed. The existing receipt no longer verifies under this code, so native approval lapses until one campaign on Spark re-freezes the ranges and records a new receipt.
next: Re-freeze the parity ranges from the three baseline replays under the judge and run one candidate campaign on Spark to renew the receipt; then add the route cases so native runs the waypoint follower in closed loop.
reason: The evaluation code changes; the checkpoint, the robot model, the requirements file and the roadmap markers remain unchanged. No result is admitted: c48_long still fails the drift limit under the judge.
